absent: Full VMCB control and save area layouts beyond the fields touched here.
ASID allocation, recycling, and collision avoidance beyond generation bump and bounds init.
AVIC enable, configuration, and teardown sequencing.
SEV and SNP guest creation, attestation, and reverse map management details.
PMU mediation contracts, counter counts, and event filtering.
Nested virtualization intercept forwarding and L1 L2 control block shadowing.
MSR permission bitmap encoding and address translation for x2APIC handling.
TSC ratio calculation, multiplier encoding, and scaling enable conditions.
Guest debug single step interaction with NMI injection beyond flag restore.
IOPM allocation, population, and sharing across virtual CPUs.

findings.text: Two host wide memory virtualization switches default to enabled and remain observable outside this file, one frozen after early init and one left mutable, allowing the rest of the host to query whether nested paging and an extended address handling mode are active.

Three host wide controls for advanced interrupt and branch sampling virtualization default to enabled and are frozen after early init, letting other host code test whether next RIP tracking, virtual interrupt masking, and branch record virtualization are permitted.

Host wide controls for intercepting firmware interrupts, enabling virtual nonmaskable interrupts, and dumping invalid control blocks default to intercept and virtual NMI enabled with dumping disabled, visible to other host code and frozen or mostly read after init.

Pause filtering exposes five early frozen tunables for threshold and window sizing, seeded from generic pause exit gap and growth constants with SVM specific window defaults, defining the starting window plus grow and shrink steps and an upper bound used when adapting to pause exit behavior.

Four file private switches for nested virtualization, virtual load store handling, time stamp scaling, and an erratum workaround for fault intercepts all default to enabled and become immutable after early init, gating optional SVM behaviors without external visibility.

Operating system visible workaround state uses a dedicated spinlock to serialize updates that shrink the advertised length to a minimum and accumulate status bits across CPUs, while a separate mutex serializes diagnostic dumps of control blocks to avoid interleaved output.

Per CPU state holds a time stamp ratio cache and a larger SVM control structure per processor, complemented by a host wide IO permission bitmap base and a small byte sequence for resume from firmware, establishing the memory anchors for virtualization enable and exit handling.

Processor matching relies on a small table that recognizes any CPU advertising the SVM feature and terminates with an empty entry, providing the identifier list used during module load to restrict operation to capable hardware.
Two descriptor type numbers are fixed for local descriptor table and 16 bit busy task state segment handling, with values two and three respectively.
Soft interrupt vector information for skipped emulation is encoded by keeping the low eight bits of the vector and placing them at bit position sixteen inside a 32 bit emulation control word.

Nested page table depth adapts to build and paging mode, selecting a five level root when five level paging is active on 64 bit builds, otherwise a four level root on 64 bit and a legacy 32 bit extended root elsewhere.

Injection of software style exceptions first ensures a usable resume address is available even when hardware omits it, preserving code base plus old and new instruction pointers alongside a marker that injection was attempted, restoring the original pointer when next RIP tracking is active and programming the hardware resume field only when the feature exists, with failure causing the event to be dropped for retry.
Exception delivery combines payload preparation with special handling for software vectors before programming the control block event fields with vector, validity, type, and error code information.

Each virtual CPU advertises workaround length as at least three and hides two bits that the host claims as fixed by interception, while conservatively reporting an early microcode erratum as present on a specific processor family when the host reports zero length and therefore no information.

Host workaround discovery treats missing capability or failed safe register reads as zero length and status, keeps the smallest length seen and the union of status bits masked to that length, and leaves state untouched when length is already zero or when newly read values add no information.

Processor compatibility is exposed as a checked entry that refuses vendors outside the two supported compatible families, CPUs lacking the virtualization feature, and hosts already running as encrypted guests, with a migration safe wrapper for general queries and a simple error returning variant for load time validation.

A translation lookaside erratum workaround touches a model specific configuration register only when the corresponding CPU bug is present, using fault tolerant accesses so nested operation is not disturbed, setting bit 47 and recording that the workaround was applied.

Per processor virtualization follows an enable path that acquires a reference, refreshes address space identifier generation to avoid stale reuse, derives identifier bounds from hardware limits and encrypted guest reservation, points firmware save state at the per CPU area, resets time scaling to default, refreshes workaround state and bug handling, and enables performance virtualization, with disable restoring defaults and releasing the reference and emergency disable only clearing the firmware save pointer.

Processor initialization zeroes per CPU state then allocates a node local save page with encrypted guest safe allocation, wires optional encrypted guest CPU state, and publishes both virtual and encrypted physical addresses, freeing the page on error, while teardown releases encrypted virtual blocks and the save page exactly once and clears published addresses.
Host state for encrypted guests with register protection is reached through the per CPU control structure, exposing the host portion of the save area for use during transitions.

Debug register handling can enable read and write interception for all general debug registers on the primary control block or clear the whole debug intercept word at once, in both cases marking intercept state dirty so hardware reloads it.
Whether a model specific register write causes an exit is determined by consulting the permission bitmap whose base is taken from the current control block after removing memory encryption masking.

Performance counter register interception stays unchanged unless mediated performance is enabled, otherwise legacy and extended counter ranges follow direct access when mediation is active for the virtual CPU and capability bits allow, with extra counters beyond the virtual CPU count always intercepted and global control registers following a separate global control need signal.

Model specific register intercept policy grants direct access to common system call and segment base registers, then conditionally adjusts interception for branch sampling, prediction control, cache flush, speculation control, Intel compatible system enter addresses, frequency counters, protected stack registers, encrypted guest extensions, and performance mediation, leaving second level address translation intercepts to on demand handling.

Pause exit window tuning grows or shrinks the current count within configured bounds using multiplicative behavior for small steps and additive behavior for large steps, marks the control block dirty and emits a trace only when the value changes, does nothing while running nested guests, and treats tuning as unexpected when pause exits are disabled in the guest.

Disabling nonmaskable interrupt single stepping always clears the internal stepping marker and, unless guest debugging already requests single stepping, restores trap and resume flag state to match what the guest had before stepping began.

Interrupt shadow state is reported as a combined blocked condition covering both flag based and stack segment move based blocking whenever any relevant bit is set in the control block interrupt state.

Host teardown releases advanced interrupt and encrypted guest resources, tears down every possible processor save area, then frees the shared IO permission bitmap pages and clears the base pointer so reuse is impossible.

Fresh segment descriptors start with zero selector and base plus a full 16 bit limit, with regular data segments marked present, usable, and writable while system segments combine presence with a caller supplied type.

Nested time stamp handling sources second level offset and scaling factor from nested control state and the per virtual CPU ratio register, while the write path updates both the primary and the active control block offsets from first and second level values and marks intercept state dirty.

A page range sharing query for encrypted guests reports unshared when the virtual machine is not a protected SNP guest, reports smallest page granularity when reverse map lookup fails or the page is not assigned, and otherwise reports the large page level recorded in the reverse map.

Diagnostic messages from this module are prefixed with the module name, and the host reserves a user return slot for auxiliary time stamp handling that starts as negative one until assigned during init.
